metadata.description: Scenario-Based Study Guide for CLF-C02 certification - validates foundational knowledge of AWS Cloud concepts, services, security, architecture, pricing, and support.

questions.title: Cloud Computing Benefits
questions.scenario: A startup is deciding whether to build their own data center or use cloud computing. They have unpredictable traffic patterns and limited upfront capital. The CTO wants to understand the key benefits of moving to the cloud.
questions.questionText: Which benefit of cloud computing allows the startup to pay only for the resources they actually use?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which pricing approach aligns with variable, unpredictable usage and zero upfront commitment.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Pay-as-you-go pricing is a fundamental benefit of cloud computing. Instead of purchasing and maintaining expensive hardware upfront, companies pay only for the compute, storage, and other resources they actually use. This converts capital expenses (CapEx) to operational expenses (OpEx) and is ideal for startups with unpredictable workloads.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• AWS offers multiple pricing models: On-Demand (pay by the hour/second), Reserved Instances (commit for 1-3 years for discounts), Spot Instances (bid on unused capacity), and Savings Plans.
  • The pay-as-you-go model eliminates the need for capacity forecasting and reduces the risk of over-provisioning or under-provisioning.
  • This model supports the AWS Well-Architected Framework's Cost Optimization pillar.

questions.title: Elasticity vs Scalability
questions.scenario: An e-commerce company experiences a 10x traffic spike during Black Friday sales, then returns to normal levels afterward. They need their infrastructure to automatically adjust to these demand changes.
questions.questionText: Which cloud computing characteristic best describes the ability to automatically scale resources up during peak demand and scale down when demand decreases?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which characteristic specifically implies automatic, dynamic adjustment — not just the ability to grow, but to shrink back too?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Elasticity is the cloud's ability to automatically scale resources up or down based on actual demand. This is different from scalability, which is the general ability to handle growth. Elasticity specifically implies automatic, dynamic adjustment - perfect for handling unpredictable traffic spikes like Black Friday sales without manual intervention.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• AWS Auto Scaling is the primary service that enables elasticity, automatically adjusting EC2 instances, ECS tasks, DynamoDB capacity, and more.
  • Elasticity helps optimize costs by scaling down during low-demand periods, avoiding paying for unused capacity.
  • True elasticity requires stateless application design so instances can be added or removed without losing data.

questions.title: Shared Responsibility Model
questions.scenario: A company is migrating their application to AWS EC2 instances. The security team wants to understand which security responsibilities belong to AWS and which belong to the customer.
questions.questionText: According to the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system on EC2 instances?

choices.text: Both AWS and the customer equally

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider the "security OF the cloud" vs. "security IN the cloud" split. Which side does guest OS patching fall on?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, AWS is responsible for "security OF the cloud" (physical infrastructure, hardware, networking), while customers are responsible for "security IN the cloud" (data, applications, OS patching, network configuration, IAM). For EC2, customers must patch and maintain the guest operating system.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• The responsibility model varies by service type: IaaS (EC2) requires more customer responsibility than PaaS (Elastic Beanstalk) or SaaS (fully managed services).
  • AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager can help automate OS patching, but the responsibility still lies with the customer.
  • For managed services like RDS or Lambda, AWS handles more of the patching responsibilities.

questions.title: AWS Global Infrastructure
questions.scenario: A company needs to deploy their application closer to customers in Asia to reduce latency. They currently have all resources in the US East region.
questions.questionText: What AWS infrastructure component should they use to deploy resources in a different geographic location?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about the largest unit of AWS global infrastructure — the one that represents a full, independent geographic deployment.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Regions are physically isolated geographic areas consisting of multiple Availability Zones. To serve customers in Asia with lower latency, the company should deploy their application to an AWS Region in Asia (like ap-northeast-1 Tokyo or ap-southeast-1 Singapore). Edge Locations are for CloudFront CDN caching, not full application deployment.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Each AWS Region has at least 3 Availability Zones (isolated data centers) for high availability.
  • Data residency and compliance requirements often dictate which Region to use.
  • Not all AWS services are available in all Regions - check service availability before choosing a Region.

questions.title: Availability Zones
questions.scenario: An architect is designing a highly available web application on AWS. They want to ensure the application continues running even if a data center experiences a power outage.
questions.questionText: What should the architect do to protect against a single data center failure?

choices.text: Deploy resources across multiple Availability Zones
Deploy resources to a single Availability Zone with backups

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: High availability comes from redundancy. What kind of redundancy protects against an entire facility losing power?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Availability Zones (AZs) are physically separate data centers within an AWS Region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking. By deploying resources across multiple AZs, if one AZ experiences an outage, the application continues running in the other AZs. This is a fundamental high availability pattern in AWS.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• AZs within a Region are connected via low-latency, high-bandwidth links, enabling synchronous replication.
  • Services like ELB, RDS Multi-AZ, and Auto Scaling can automatically distribute resources across AZs.
  • For disaster recovery across geographic areas, use multiple Regions instead of just multiple AZs.

questions.title: Well-Architected Framework Pillars
questions.scenario: A solutions architect is reviewing an application design against AWS best practices. They need to ensure the architecture addresses all key areas of the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: One of these choices was never part of the framework. Think about what the real pillars actually focus on — does each option sound like a formal pillar?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: The AWS Well-Architected Framework has six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability. "Speed and Velocity" is not a pillar - while agility is a benefit of cloud computing, it's not a formal Well-Architected pillar.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Sustainability was added as the sixth pillar in 2021, focusing on environmental impact.
  • AWS provides the Well-Architected Tool in the console to review workloads against these pillars.
  • Each pillar has design principles, best practices, and questions to evaluate your architecture.

questions.title: Compute Service Selection
questions.scenario: A developer needs to run a simple web application that handles HTTP requests. They want the simplest deployment with minimal infrastructure management and automatic scaling.
questions.questionText: Which AWS compute service provides a fully managed platform for deploying web applications with automatic scaling and no server management?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which service sits at the PaaS level — you upload code, and it handles the rest without you touching servers.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) that abstracts infrastructure management. You simply upload your code, and Beanstalk handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, auto-scaling, and health monitoring. It supports multiple languages and frameworks while still allowing access to underlying resources if needed.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Elastic Beanstalk uses EC2 instances behind the scenes but manages them automatically.
  • You can customize the environment using configuration files (.ebextensions) or by accessing the underlying resources.
  • Beanstalk supports deployment strategies like rolling updates and blue/green deployments.

questions.title: Serverless Compute
questions.scenario: A company wants to run code in response to events like file uploads to S3 or API calls. They don't want to provision or manage any servers and only want to pay when the code runs.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service allows running code without provisioning servers and charges only for compute time consumed?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which compute option is truly serverless — no instances to provision, billed only while your code executes?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Lambda is a serverless, event-driven compute service. You upload your code, and Lambda automatically runs it in response to triggers (S3 events, API Gateway requests, CloudWatch events, etc.). There are no servers to manage, and you pay only for the compute time consumed - billing is per millisecond of execution time.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Lambda functions can run for up to 15 minutes and have memory allocations from 128 MB to 10 GB.
  • Lambda@Edge allows running functions at CloudFront edge locations for lower latency.
  • Lambda supports multiple runtimes (Node.js, Python, Java, Go, .NET, Ruby) and custom runtimes.

questions.title: Object Storage
questions.scenario: A media company needs to store large video files that will be accessed frequently by users worldwide. They need a highly durable storage solution that can scale to petabytes of data.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service is best suited for storing and retrieving large amounts of unstructured data like images, videos, and documents?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which storage type is designed for unstructured data accessed via HTTP — not a file system, not a disk volume.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon S3 is an object storage service offering industry-leading durability (99.999999999% - 11 nines), availability, and scalability. It's ideal for storing unstructured data like media files, backups, and static websites. S3 can store unlimited objects and integrates with CloudFront for global content delivery.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• S3 offers multiple storage classes: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier, and Glacier Deep Archive.
  • S3 is not a file system - it's object storage with a flat structure (buckets and objects with keys).
  • S3 Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront edge locations to speed up uploads from distant locations.

questions.title: Block Storage for EC2
questions.scenario: A database administrator needs persistent block storage for an EC2 instance running a MySQL database. The storage must persist even if the instance is stopped.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides persistent block storage volumes for EC2 instances?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The question asks for block-level storage that survives instance stops. Which service type attaches as a virtual disk drive?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon EBS provides block-level storage volumes that persist independently from EC2 instance lifecycle. Unlike instance store (ephemeral storage), EBS volumes retain data when instances are stopped or terminated (if configured). EBS is ideal for databases, file systems, and any workload requiring persistent, low-latency storage.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• EBS volume types include gp3/gp2 (general purpose SSD), io2/io1 (provisioned IOPS SSD), st1 (throughput optimized HDD), and sc1 (cold HDD).
  • EBS volumes are automatically replicated within their Availability Zone for durability.
  • EBS Snapshots provide point-in-time backups stored in S3, enabling cross-AZ and cross-Region copies.

questions.title: Relational Database Service
questions.scenario: A company wants to run a PostgreSQL database in the cloud but doesn't want to manage patching, backups, or high availability configuration. They need a managed solution.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a managed relational database that handles routine maintenance tasks?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Look for the service specifically designed to run relational engines like PostgreSQL in a managed way. Not a cache, not a warehouse, not NoSQL.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service supporting multiple engines: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, and Aurora. RDS handles time-consuming tasks like hardware provisioning, database setup, patching, and backups, allowing you to focus on application development rather than database administration.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• RDS Multi-AZ deployments provide high availability with automatic failover to a standby in another AZ.
  • Read Replicas enable read scaling and can be promoted to standalone databases.
  • Amazon Aurora is an AWS-designed database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, offering better performance and availability.

questions.title: NoSQL Database
questions.scenario: A gaming company needs a database for storing player session data. Requirements include single-digit millisecond latency, automatic scaling, and no database administration overhead.
questions.questionText: Which AWS database service is a fully managed NoSQL database that provides fast and predictable performance with seamless scalability?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The key requirements are NoSQL, single-digit millisecond latency, and zero admin overhead. Which service is built for key-value workloads at scale?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless, fully managed NoSQL database that delivers single-digit millisecond latency. It automatically scales throughput capacity based on demand and requires zero database administration. DynamoDB is ideal for gaming, IoT, mobile apps, and any workload requiring consistent low-latency data access.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• DynamoDB supports both key-value and document data models with flexible schemas.
  • DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) provides microsecond latency for read-heavy workloads via in-memory caching.
  • Global Tables enable multi-region, multi-active replication for globally distributed applications.

questions.title: Content Delivery Network
questions.scenario: A company hosts their website in the US but has users globally. Users in Asia and Europe experience slow page load times due to latency.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service can cache content at edge locations worldwide to reduce latency for global users?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The problem is latency for distant users. Think about which service caches copies of content at locations physically closer to those users.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon CloudFront is a Content Delivery Network (CDN) that caches static and dynamic content at over 450 edge locations worldwide. When users request content, CloudFront serves it from the nearest edge location, dramatically reducing latency. CloudFront integrates with S3, EC2, ELB, and custom origins.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• CloudFront supports Lambda@Edge for running code at edge locations to customize content delivery.
  • CloudFront can serve both static content (images, CSS, JS) and dynamic content (API responses).
  • CloudFront provides DDoS protection through integration with AWS Shield.

questions.title: DNS Service
questions.scenario: A company needs to register a domain name and route traffic to their AWS resources. They also want health checks to automatically route traffic away from unhealthy endpoints.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides DNS management, domain registration, and health checking capabilities?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The question bundles three needs: domain registration, name-to-IP resolution, and health checks. Which single service covers all three?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable DNS web service. It provides three main functions: domain registration, DNS routing (translating domain names to IP addresses), and health checking of resources. Route 53 can route traffic based on latency, geography, or weighted distribution, and automatically remove unhealthy endpoints from DNS responses.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Route 53 supports various routing policies: Simple, Weighted, Latency-based, Failover, Geolocation, Geoproximity, and Multivalue Answer.
  • The name "Route 53" refers to TCP/UDP port 53, the standard port for DNS.
  • Route 53 is one of the few AWS services with 100% availability SLA.

questions.title: Virtual Private Cloud
questions.scenario: A company wants to launch AWS resources in a logically isolated network where they control IP addressing, subnets, and routing. They need both public-facing web servers and private database servers.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service allows you to create an isolated virtual network with complete control over the networking environment?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which service gives you your own logically isolated section of the cloud with full control over networking — IP ranges, subnets, gateways?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon VPC enables you to launch AWS resources in a logically isolated virtual network. You define the IP address range, create subnets, configure route tables, and set up network gateways. Public subnets have routes to the internet (via an Internet Gateway), while private subnets are isolated. VPC provides the foundation for network security in AWS.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• VPC components include subnets, route tables, internet gateways, NAT gateways, security groups, and network ACLs.
  • VPC Peering connects two VPCs for private traffic, while Transit Gateway simplifies connecting multiple VPCs.
  • VPC Flow Logs capture information about IP traffic for monitoring and troubleshooting.

questions.title: Identity and Access Management
questions.scenario: An administrator needs to create user accounts for new employees and grant them specific permissions to access only the AWS resources they need for their job.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service is used to manage users, groups, and permissions for accessing AWS resources?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about the core service for controlling who can access what in AWS — users, groups, roles, and policies all live here.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS IAM enables you to manage access to AWS services and resources securely. You create IAM users for individuals, organize them into groups, and attach policies that define their permissions. IAM follows the principle of least privilege - granting only the permissions needed to perform a task.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• IAM is global - users, groups, and roles are not region-specific.
  • IAM Roles allow AWS services, applications, or federated users to assume temporary credentials.
  • IAM policies are JSON documents specifying Effect (Allow/Deny), Actions, Resources, and optional Conditions.

questions.title: Root User Security
questions.scenario: A startup just created their first AWS account. The founder has been using the root account credentials for all daily tasks including launching EC2 instances and managing S3 buckets.
questions.questionText: What is the AWS best practice regarding the use of the root user account?

choices.text: Use root for all tasks to ensure full access to all resources
Share root credentials with all administrators
Delete the root account after creating IAM users
Use root only for account management tasks that require it, and create IAM users for daily tasks

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider the principle of least privilege. Should the most powerful account be used for routine daily operations?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS best practice is to avoid using the root user for daily tasks. The root user has unrestricted access to all resources and cannot be limited by IAM policies. Instead, create IAM users or roles with only the permissions needed. Reserve root for tasks that require it, like changing account settings, closing the account, or restoring IAM access.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Always enable MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) on the root account for additional security.
  • Do not create access keys for the root user - if they exist, delete them.
  • Tasks requiring root include: changing account name/email, changing support plans, and closing the account.

questions.title: Multi-Factor Authentication
questions.scenario: A security audit recommends adding an additional layer of security beyond passwords for AWS console access. The auditors want protection even if passwords are compromised.
questions.questionText: Which security feature requires users to provide a password plus a code from an authentication device when signing in?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The question describes "something you know" plus "something you have." Which security feature combines two different proof-of-identity methods?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds an extra layer of protection by requiring something you know (password) and something you have (authentication device). Even if a password is compromised, an attacker cannot access the account without the MFA device. AWS supports virtual MFA apps, hardware keys, and U2F security keys.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• MFA can be required for specific IAM actions using policy conditions (aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent).
  • AWS supports TOTP-compatible virtual MFA apps (Google Authenticator, Authy) and hardware devices.
  • MFA should be enabled on all privileged accounts, especially the root user.

questions.title: Encryption at Rest
questions.scenario: A healthcare company must encrypt all data stored in AWS to comply with HIPAA regulations. They need a managed service to create and control encryption keys.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service helps you create and manage cryptographic keys for encrypting data at rest?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Focus on the word "keys." Which service is purpose-built for creating, storing, and controlling the cryptographic keys used in encryption?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) is a managed service for creating and controlling cryptographic keys. KMS integrates with most AWS services (S3, EBS, RDS, etc.) to easily encrypt data at rest. You can create customer-managed keys, set key policies, and audit key usage through CloudTrail.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• KMS keys (formerly CMKs) can be AWS managed, customer managed, or custom key store (CloudHSM).
  • KMS supports automatic key rotation for customer-managed keys (annually).
  • Envelope encryption is used: KMS encrypts a data key, which encrypts your data.

questions.title: Security Groups
questions.scenario: An administrator needs to control which network traffic is allowed to reach EC2 instances. They want to allow HTTP traffic from the internet but block all other inbound traffic.
questions.questionText: Which AWS feature acts as a virtual firewall for EC2 instances to control inbound and outbound traffic?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about what operates at the instance level as a stateful firewall — not a subnet-level or application-level filter.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Security Groups are stateful virtual firewalls that control traffic to and from EC2 instances. You define inbound and outbound rules specifying allowed protocols, ports, and source/destination. Security Groups are stateful, meaning if you allow inbound traffic, the response traffic is automatically allowed.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Security Groups have implicit deny - only explicitly allowed traffic is permitted.
  • You can reference other Security Groups as sources, enabling secure communication between tiers.
  • Network ACLs are stateless and operate at the subnet level, providing an additional layer of security.

questions.title: DDoS Protection
questions.scenario: A company's web application has been experiencing distributed denial-of-service attacks. They need protection against common network and application layer attacks.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides automatic protection against DDoS attacks for all AWS customers at no additional cost?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The key qualifiers are "automatic," "all customers," and "no additional cost." Which DDoS service tier is enabled by default?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Shield is a managed DDoS protection service. Shield Standard is automatically enabled for all AWS customers at no additional cost and protects against common, most frequently occurring network and transport layer attacks. Shield Advanced provides additional protection, 24/7 DDoS response team access, and cost protection for scaling.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Shield Standard protects against Layer 3/4 attacks like SYN floods and UDP reflection attacks.
  • Shield Advanced adds Layer 7 (application layer) protection and integrates with AWS WAF.
  • Shield Advanced provides real-time visibility and access to AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT).

questions.title: Compliance Programs
questions.scenario: A financial services company needs to ensure their AWS infrastructure meets regulatory requirements. They need documentation showing AWS's compliance with various standards.
questions.questionText: Which AWS resource provides access to AWS compliance reports and certifications like SOC, PCI-DSS, and ISO?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The company needs to download compliance documentation like SOC and PCI reports. Which portal is the self-service source for those documents?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Artifact is a portal providing on-demand access to AWS's security and compliance documents. You can download AWS's SOC reports, PCI-DSS attestations, ISO certifications, and other compliance documentation. Artifact also allows you to review, accept, and manage agreements like the Business Associate Addendum (BAA) for HIPAA.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• AWS Artifact is free to use and available in the AWS Management Console.
  • Compliance reports are produced by third-party auditors who verify AWS's controls.
  • AWS maintains compliance with over 90 security standards and compliance certifications globally.

questions.title: Threat Detection
questions.scenario: A security team wants to continuously monitor their AWS accounts for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior, such as unusual API calls or potentially compromised instances.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service uses machine learning to detect threats and malicious activity in your AWS environment?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which service uses ML to analyze logs (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS) and surface suspicious account or network behavior.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon GuardDuty is an intelligent threat detection service that analyzes AWS CloudTrail logs, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs to identify threats. It uses machine learning, anomaly detection, and integrated threat intelligence to detect issues like compromised instances, reconnaissance, and account compromise. GuardDuty requires no infrastructure to manage.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• GuardDuty generates findings categorized by severity (Low, Medium, High) with remediation recommendations.
  • It can detect cryptocurrency mining, command and control activity, and data exfiltration attempts.
  • GuardDuty integrates with Security Hub for centralized security findings management.

questions.title: Free Tier
questions.scenario: A developer wants to learn AWS without incurring costs. They want to understand what services and resources are available for free.
questions.questionText: Which statement about the AWS Free Tier is correct?

choices.text: The Free Tier includes some always-free services, 12-month free trials, and short-term trials
All AWS services are free for the first year
Free Tier is only available for enterprise accounts
Free Tier requires a minimum monthly commitment

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider whether the Free Tier is one-size-fits-all or has multiple offer categories with different durations and eligibility.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: The AWS Free Tier has three offer types: Always Free (like Lambda's 1M free requests/month, DynamoDB's 25GB), 12 Months Free (like 750 hours/month of EC2 t2.micro, 5GB S3 storage), and short-term trials for specific services. Not all services are included, and usage beyond free tier limits incurs charges.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Set up billing alerts and budgets to avoid unexpected charges when exceeding Free Tier limits.
  • Some services like VPC, IAM, and Consolidated Billing are always free to use.
  • Free Tier is available to new and existing AWS accounts (though 12-month offers only apply to new accounts).

questions.title: Pricing Models
questions.scenario: A company runs steady-state workloads that will run continuously for at least one year. They want to reduce costs compared to on-demand pricing.
questions.questionText: Which EC2 pricing option provides significant discounts in exchange for committing to use a specific instance type for 1 or 3 years?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The scenario is a steady, predictable workload running for at least a year. Which pricing model trades commitment for a discount?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Reserved Instances provide significant discounts (up to 72%) compared to On-Demand pricing when you commit to using EC2 for 1 or 3 years. They're ideal for steady-state, predictable workloads. Payment options include All Upfront (biggest discount), Partial Upfront, and No Upfront. Standard RIs offer the best discount; Convertible RIs allow changing instance families.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Savings Plans offer similar discounts with more flexibility across instance families and services.
  • Spot Instances can save up to 90% but can be interrupted with 2-minute notice.
  • Reserved capacity applies to a specific AZ, while regional RIs provide AZ flexibility.

questions.title: Cost Explorer
questions.scenario: A finance team needs to analyze their AWS spending patterns over the past 6 months and forecast future costs based on historical usage.
questions.questionText: Which AWS tool allows you to visualize, understand, and manage your AWS costs and usage over time?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The team needs to look backward at historical spending and forecast forward. Which tool provides graphical cost analysis over time?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Cost Explorer is a tool for visualizing and analyzing AWS costs and usage. It provides graphs showing spending patterns over time, allows filtering by service, account, or tags, and can forecast future costs based on historical data. Cost Explorer helps identify trends, anomalies, and cost optimization opportunities.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Cost Explorer retains 12 months of historical data and can forecast up to 12 months ahead.
  • It provides recommendations for Reserved Instances and Savings Plans based on your usage.
  • Cost Explorer API enables programmatic access for custom reporting and automation.

questions.title: AWS Budgets
questions.scenario: A manager wants to be notified when their team's AWS spending exceeds $1,000 per month so they can take action before costs get out of control.
questions.questionText: Which AWS feature allows you to set custom spending thresholds and receive alerts when costs exceed those limits?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The manager wants proactive alerts at a specific dollar threshold. Which tool lets you define spending limits and get notified?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Budgets allows you to set custom budgets for costs, usage, Reserved Instance utilization, and Savings Plans coverage. You can configure alerts to notify you via email or SNS when actual or forecasted amounts exceed thresholds. Budgets can also trigger automated actions like applying IAM policies or stopping EC2 instances.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• AWS Budgets can create cost, usage, reservation, or Savings Plans budgets.
  • Budget Actions can automatically respond to budget thresholds (e.g., restrict IAM permissions).
  • The first two budgets per account are free; additional budgets cost $0.02/day each.

questions.title: Pricing Calculator
questions.scenario: A solutions architect needs to estimate the monthly cost of a proposed AWS architecture before deploying any resources. The estimate will be presented to stakeholders for budget approval.
questions.questionText: Which AWS tool helps estimate the cost of AWS services before you start using them?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The architect needs a cost estimate before deploying anything. Which tool lets you model a proposed architecture and see projected costs?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Pricing Calculator is a web-based planning tool that lets you estimate the cost of AWS services based on your requirements. You configure services with expected usage (instance types, storage, data transfer, etc.), and it generates a detailed cost estimate. Estimates can be saved, shared, and exported for budget planning.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• The Pricing Calculator replaced the older Simple Monthly Calculator and TCO Calculator.
  • Estimates include all pricing dimensions: compute, storage, data transfer, requests, etc.
  • You can create multiple scenarios to compare different architecture options.

questions.title: AWS Organizations
questions.scenario: A company has multiple AWS accounts for different departments (development, testing, production). They want to centrally manage billing, apply policies across accounts, and get volume discounts.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service allows you to centrally manage multiple AWS accounts, consolidate billing, and apply policies?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which service is designed specifically for managing a fleet of AWS accounts — billing, policies, and governance in one place.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Organizations allows you to create an organization to centrally manage multiple AWS accounts. It provides consolidated billing (one bill for all accounts), Service Control Policies (SCPs) for governance, and enables sharing of Reserved Instances. Organizations helps achieve volume discounts as usage is aggregated across all accounts.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Service Control Policies (SCPs) set permission guardrails for member accounts.
  • Organizational Units (OUs) group accounts for applying policies hierarchically.
  • AWS Control Tower builds on Organizations to set up and govern a secure multi-account environment.

questions.title: Support Plans
questions.scenario: A company running production workloads on AWS needs 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers for technical issues and wants guidance from a Technical Account Manager.
questions.questionText: Which AWS Support plan provides a Technical Account Manager (TAM) and 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Only one support tier includes a designated person who provides proactive architectural guidance. Which tier is that?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS offers four support plans: Basic (free), Developer, Business, and Enterprise. Enterprise Support includes a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), Concierge Support Team, 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers via phone/chat/email, and 15-minute response time for critical issues. Business Support offers 24/7 support but no TAM.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• TAMs provide proactive guidance, architectural reviews, and help optimize your AWS environment.
  • Enterprise Support also includes Infrastructure Event Management for planned events.
  • Enterprise On-Ramp is a lower-cost option with a pool of TAMs instead of a designated one.

questions.title: Load Balancing
questions.scenario: A web application runs on multiple EC2 instances. The team needs to distribute incoming traffic across all instances and automatically route traffic away from unhealthy instances.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets like EC2 instances?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The goal is to spread incoming requests evenly across a pool of instances and skip unhealthy ones. Which service does that?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) automatically distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets (EC2 instances, containers, IP addresses) in one or more Availability Zones. ELB performs health checks and routes traffic only to healthy targets. AWS offers three types: Application Load Balancer (HTTP/HTTPS), Network Load Balancer (TCP/UDP), and Gateway Load Balancer.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Application Load Balancer (ALB) operates at Layer 7 and supports path-based and host-based routing.
  • Network Load Balancer (NLB) operates at Layer 4 and can handle millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency.
  • ELB integrates with Auto Scaling to add or remove instances based on demand.

questions.title: Auto Scaling
questions.scenario: An e-commerce website experiences variable traffic throughout the day. The team wants to automatically add EC2 instances during peak hours and remove them during low traffic periods.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances based on demand?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The need is to add instances when traffic spikes and remove them when it drops. Which service manages that lifecycle automatically?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling helps ensure you have the right number of EC2 instances to handle your application load. You define minimum, maximum, and desired capacity, along with scaling policies based on metrics like CPU utilization. Auto Scaling automatically launches or terminates instances to match demand, maintaining availability while optimizing costs.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Scaling policies can be target tracking (maintain a metric), step scaling, or scheduled.
  • Launch templates or launch configurations define the instance configuration for new instances.
  • Predictive scaling uses machine learning to forecast demand and pre-scale before traffic spikes.

questions.title: Monitoring Service
questions.scenario: An operations team needs to monitor their AWS resources, collect metrics, set alarms, and automatically react to changes in their applications.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides monitoring and observability for AWS resources and applications?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which service collects metrics, stores logs, and lets you set alarms that trigger actions when thresholds are breached?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon CloudWatch is AWS's monitoring and observability service. It collects metrics from AWS resources (EC2, RDS, Lambda, etc.), stores logs, creates dashboards, and triggers alarms based on thresholds. CloudWatch can automatically trigger actions like Auto Scaling or SNS notifications when metrics breach thresholds.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• CloudWatch Logs collects, monitors, and analyzes log files from AWS services and applications.
  • CloudWatch Events (now EventBridge) responds to state changes in AWS resources.
  • CloudWatch Container Insights provides monitoring for containerized applications on ECS and EKS.

questions.title: API Activity Logging
questions.scenario: A security team needs to track who made changes to AWS resources, including what API calls were made, by whom, and when. This is required for compliance auditing.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service logs API calls and provides a history of AWS account activity?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The security team needs a "who did what, when" audit log of every API call. Which service records that activity history?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS CloudTrail is an auditing service that records API calls made in your AWS account. It captures who made the call, from what IP address, at what time, and what resources were affected. CloudTrail logs are essential for security analysis, compliance auditing, and operational troubleshooting. Logs can be stored in S3 and analyzed with Athena.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• CloudTrail captures both management events (control plane) and data events (data plane operations).
  • CloudTrail Insights identifies unusual API activity patterns automatically.
  • CloudTrail logs can be integrated with CloudWatch Logs for real-time monitoring and alerting.

questions.title: Infrastructure as Code
questions.scenario: A DevOps team wants to define their AWS infrastructure in code so they can version control it, review changes, and deploy consistently across environments.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service allows you to model and provision AWS resources using templates written in JSON or YAML?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about Infrastructure as Code — which AWS-native service turns a declarative template into a running stack of resources?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS CloudFormation is an Infrastructure as Code (IaC) service that lets you define AWS resources in JSON or YAML templates. CloudFormation provisions and manages resources as a stack, handling dependencies and enabling consistent deployments. Templates can be version-controlled, reviewed, and reused across environments (dev, test, prod).

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• CloudFormation stacks can be nested for modular, reusable architectures.
  • Change sets preview what CloudFormation will change before applying updates.
  • CloudFormation drift detection identifies resources that have been modified outside of CloudFormation.

questions.title: Message Queuing
questions.scenario: A distributed application needs to decouple its components. The front-end service should send messages to a queue, and the back-end service should process them asynchronously without losing messages.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a fully managed message queuing service for decoupling application components?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The pattern is a queue between producers and consumers so they don't need to run simultaneously. Which managed service implements that?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon SQS is a fully managed message queuing service that enables you to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. SQS eliminates the complexity of managing message infrastructure. It offers two queue types: Standard (maximum throughput, at-least-once delivery) and FIFO (exactly-once processing, ordered messages).

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SQS Standard queues support nearly unlimited throughput; FIFO queues support up to 3,000 messages/second with batching.
  • Dead-letter queues capture messages that can't be processed for debugging.
  • SQS integrates with Lambda for serverless message processing.

questions.title: Pub/Sub Messaging
questions.scenario: An application needs to send notifications to multiple subscribers simultaneously - email notifications, SMS messages, and triggering Lambda functions - all from a single published message.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a pub/sub messaging paradigm where a single message can be delivered to multiple subscribers?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The key is one message reaching many subscribers at once — a fan-out pattern. Which service uses topics to push to multiple endpoints?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon SNS is a fully managed pub/sub messaging service. Publishers send messages to topics, and SNS delivers those messages to all subscribers of the topic. Subscribers can be SQS queues, Lambda functions, HTTP endpoints, email addresses, SMS numbers, or mobile push notifications. This enables fan-out patterns where one event triggers multiple actions.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SNS + SQS (fan-out pattern) allows one message to be processed by multiple independent consumers.
  • SNS Message Filtering lets subscribers receive only a subset of messages based on attributes.
  • SNS FIFO topics work with SQS FIFO queues for ordered, exactly-once delivery.

questions.title: Container Orchestration
questions.scenario: A company wants to run Docker containers in AWS without managing the underlying servers. They need a fully serverless option for running containers.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service allows you to run containers without managing servers or clusters?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The company wants to run containers with zero server management. Which option abstracts away the cluster infrastructure entirely?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers. With Fargate, you don't need to provision or manage EC2 instances - you just define your container requirements (CPU, memory), and Fargate handles the infrastructure. Fargate works with both Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS, allowing serverless container deployment with either orchestrator.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Fargate pricing is based on vCPU and memory resources used per second.
  • Fargate provides task-level isolation for security, as each task runs in its own kernel.
  • Fargate Spot provides up to 70% discount for fault-tolerant workloads.

questions.title: Managed Kubernetes
questions.scenario: A team with Kubernetes expertise wants to run containerized applications on AWS. They want AWS to manage the Kubernetes control plane while they focus on deploying workloads.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a managed Kubernetes control plane?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The team already uses Kubernetes. Which AWS service runs the control plane for them so they focus only on workloads?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon EKS is a managed Kubernetes service that runs the Kubernetes control plane across multiple Availability Zones, eliminating the need to install, operate, and maintain your own control plane. EKS is certified Kubernetes conformant, so you can use existing Kubernetes tools and plugins. Worker nodes can run on EC2 or Fargate.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• EKS automatically patches and updates the control plane (with your approval).
  • EKS integrates with AWS services like IAM for authentication, VPC for networking, and CloudWatch for monitoring.
  • EKS Anywhere allows running EKS on-premises with consistent tooling.

questions.title: Data Warehousing
questions.scenario: A business intelligence team needs to analyze large volumes of historical sales data. They need a data warehouse solution optimized for complex analytical queries across petabytes of data.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service is a fully managed data warehouse designed for analytics workloads?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think data warehouse, not transactional database. Which service is optimized for running complex analytical queries across petabytes?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Redshift is a fast, fully managed cloud data warehouse that makes it simple to analyze data using standard SQL and business intelligence tools. Redshift uses columnar storage, data compression, and parallel query execution to deliver fast query performance on petabytes of data. It integrates with popular BI tools like Tableau and QuickSight.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Redshift Spectrum allows querying data directly in S3 without loading it into Redshift.
  • Redshift Serverless automatically provisions and scales data warehouse capacity.
  • Redshift uses massively parallel processing (MPP) architecture for fast analytical queries.

questions.title: Trusted Advisor
questions.scenario: A cloud administrator wants recommendations to optimize their AWS environment for cost, performance, security, and fault tolerance based on AWS best practices.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides real-time guidance to help provision resources following AWS best practices?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which service acts like an automated consultant, scanning your account and recommending improvements across cost, performance, security, and more?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Trusted Advisor is an online resource that inspects your AWS environment and provides real-time recommendations based on best practices. It analyzes your accounts across five categories: cost optimization (unused resources), performance (over-provisioning), security (open security groups), fault tolerance (no backups), and service limits. Basic checks are free; full checks require Business or Enterprise Support.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• All customers get access to 7 core Trusted Advisor checks for free.
  • Business and Enterprise Support unlock all Trusted Advisor checks (over 100).
  • Trusted Advisor integrates with CloudWatch for alerting on check status changes.

questions.title: Hybrid Cloud Connectivity
questions.scenario: A company with an on-premises data center needs a dedicated, private network connection to AWS that doesn't traverse the public internet. They require consistent network performance for latency-sensitive applications.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a dedicated private connection between your data center and AWS?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The requirement is a private, dedicated link that bypasses the public internet entirely. Which service provides that physical connectivity?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated network connection between your on-premises data center and AWS. Unlike VPN (which uses encrypted tunnels over the internet), Direct Connect provides a private connection that offers more consistent network performance, reduced bandwidth costs, and a more reliable experience for hybrid workloads. It's ideal for large-scale data transfer and latency-sensitive applications.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Direct Connect offers speeds from 50 Mbps to 100 Gbps through dedicated connections or hosted connections.
  • Direct Connect Gateway enables access to VPCs in multiple regions from a single Direct Connect connection.
  • For resilience, use multiple Direct Connect connections or combine with VPN as backup.

questions.title: Database Migration
questions.scenario: A company needs to migrate their on-premises Oracle database to Amazon RDS. They want a service that simplifies the migration process and minimizes downtime.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service helps migrate databases to AWS quickly and securely with minimal downtime?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The goal is moving a database to AWS while keeping the source running during the migration. Which service specializes in that?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) helps you migrate databases to AWS quickly and securely. The source database remains fully operational during migration, minimizing downtime. DMS supports migrations between same database engines (homogeneous) or different engines (heterogeneous, using AWS Schema Conversion Tool). It works with on-premises, EC2, and RDS databases.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• DMS supports continuous data replication for ongoing sync between source and target.
  • AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) converts schema for heterogeneous migrations (e.g., Oracle to PostgreSQL).
  • DMS can migrate to Amazon RDS, Aurora, Redshift, S3, DynamoDB, and more.

questions.title: Machine Learning Service
questions.scenario: A team wants to build, train, and deploy machine learning models but needs a fully managed platform that simplifies the ML workflow.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a fully managed platform for building, training, and deploying machine learning models?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which service provides the full ML lifecycle — data labeling, model training, tuning, and deployment — in one managed platform?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon SageMaker is a fully managed machine learning service that provides every developer and data scientist with the ability to build, train, and deploy ML models quickly. SageMaker removes the heavy lifting from each step of the ML workflow, including labeling data, building models, training, tuning, and deployment. It includes built-in algorithms and supports popular frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SageMaker Studio provides a web-based IDE for the complete ML workflow.
  • SageMaker Autopilot automatically builds, trains, and tunes ML models.
  • SageMaker supports multiple deployment options: real-time inference, batch transform, and serverless inference.

questions.title: Secrets Management
questions.scenario: A developer needs to securely store database credentials and API keys used by their application. They want the secrets to be encrypted and automatically rotated.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service helps you securely store, rotate, and manage access to secrets like database credentials and API keys?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The developer needs encrypted storage with automatic rotation for credentials. Which service is purpose-built for managing secrets?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Secrets Manager is a service for managing secrets used by applications. It securely stores secrets (encrypted with KMS), provides automatic rotation capabilities for supported databases (RDS, Redshift, DocumentDB), and enables fine-grained access control through IAM policies. Applications retrieve secrets via API calls, eliminating hardcoded credentials.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Secrets Manager can automatically rotate secrets on a schedule without application changes.
  • Parameter Store (free) is an alternative for simpler use cases without automatic rotation.
  • Secrets are versioned, enabling rollback if needed.

questions.title: Edge Computing
questions.scenario: A manufacturing company needs to process IoT sensor data locally at their factory with minimal latency, while still integrating with AWS cloud services for analytics.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service allows you to run compute, messaging, and data caching locally at edge locations?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The factory needs AWS compute on-site with minimal latency. Which service physically extends AWS infrastructure into your own facility?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS Outposts is a fully managed service that extends AWS infrastructure, services, APIs, and tools to your premises. You get the same hardware and software used in AWS data centers, enabling local processing with low latency while maintaining a consistent hybrid experience. Outposts supports EC2, EBS, ECS, EKS, RDS, and other services locally.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Outposts is available in two form factors: 42U racks and smaller 1U/2U servers.
  • Local Gateway enables connectivity between Outposts and on-premises networks.
  • Data residency: data stays on Outposts locally but can sync with the AWS Region.

questions.title: Web Application Firewall
questions.scenario: A company's web application is being targeted by SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. They need a solution to filter malicious web traffic before it reaches their application.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service helps protect web applications from common web exploits like SQL injection and cross-site scripting?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The attacks are application-layer exploits (SQL injection, XSS). Which service filters HTTP traffic with customizable rules?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that helps protect web applications from common exploits that could affect availability, compromise security, or consume excessive resources. You create rules to filter traffic based on conditions like IP addresses, HTTP headers, URI strings, and SQL injection or XSS patterns. WAF integrates with CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, and AppSync.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• AWS Managed Rules provide pre-configured protection against common threats like OWASP Top 10.
  • WAF provides real-time visibility into web traffic through CloudWatch metrics.
  • Bot Control helps manage bot traffic by blocking or rate-limiting automated requests.

questions.title: File Storage
questions.scenario: Multiple EC2 instances in different Availability Zones need shared access to the same file system. They need a fully managed NFS file system that scales automatically.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a scalable, fully managed NFS file system for use with EC2 instances?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Multiple instances across AZs need concurrent access to the same files via NFS. Which storage service supports that shared access pattern?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon EFS is a fully managed, elastic NFS file system designed for use with AWS Cloud services and on-premises resources. Unlike EBS (which attaches to a single instance), EFS can be mounted concurrently by thousands of EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. EFS automatically scales storage capacity as files are added or removed.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• EFS offers Standard and Infrequent Access storage classes with lifecycle management.
  • EFS supports NFS v4.0 and v4.1 protocols with POSIX permissions.
  • EFS can be accessed from on-premises via AWS Direct Connect or VPN.

questions.title: Cost Allocation Tags
questions.scenario: A company with multiple projects running on AWS needs to track costs by project for internal billing. They want to categorize resources and see spending broken down by project.
questions.questionText: What AWS feature allows you to categorize resources and track costs by project, department, or environment?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about how you label resources with key-value metadata so that billing reports can break down spending by project or team.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Cost allocation tags are key-value pairs you assign to AWS resources. After activating tags in the Billing console, they appear in Cost Explorer and Cost and Usage Reports, enabling you to track costs by project, department, environment, or any custom category. AWS also provides generated cost allocation tags (like aws:createdBy) that are automatically added.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• User-defined tags must be activated in Billing console to appear in cost reports.
  • AWS-generated tags (like aws:createdBy) are automatically applied and can be activated.
  • Tag policies in AWS Organizations can enforce consistent tagging across accounts.

questions.title: Disaster Recovery Strategies
questions.scenario: A company needs to implement disaster recovery for their critical application. They want the lowest possible recovery time objective (RTO) but need to balance cost.
questions.questionText: Which disaster recovery strategy provides the fastest recovery time but at the highest cost?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider the DR spectrum from cheapest/slowest to most expensive/fastest. Which strategy has everything already running, so there is nothing to "recover"?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AWS defines four DR strategies with increasing cost and decreasing RTO: Backup and Restore (cheapest, slowest recovery), Pilot Light (core components running), Warm Standby (scaled-down version running), and Multi-site Active/Active (full production in multiple regions). Multi-site provides near-zero RTO since traffic is already distributed, but requires running full infrastructure in multiple regions.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• RTO (Recovery Time Objective): how quickly you need to recover after a disaster.
  • RPO (Recovery Point Objective): how much data loss is acceptable (time since last backup).
  • AWS services like Route 53 (health checks), Global Accelerator, and Aurora Global Database support multi-region architectures.
